gates.title: Polynomial form, identities, area modelling, and linear-root relations

canonical_concepts.statement: A polynomial in one variable is a finite sum of real-coefficient terms whose exponents are non-negative integers; the leading coefficient of a nonzero degree-n polynomial is nonzero.
Binomial-square and difference-of-squares identities are consequences of distributivity, including the cross terms or their cancellation.
A rectangular area model multiplies two valid side lengths and therefore has square units.
For p(x)=ax+b with a nonzero, the constant term is b and the unique zero is -b/a.

relations.meaning: Standard polynomial form in one variable x as a finite sum of terms whose exponents are non-negative integers.
Expansion of a binomial square via distributivity yields both cross products, which combine to 2ab.
conditions: Holds for all a, b in R

relations.meaning: A difference of two squares factors into conjugate binomials because the cross terms cancel.
conditions: Holds for all a, b in R

relations.expression: p(x) = ax + b, a != 0, zero at x = -b/a
relations.meaning: A degree-one polynomial has constant term b and exactly one real zero at -b/a.

relations.expression: Area(x) = (x + a)(x + b) = x^2 + (a + b)x + ab
relations.meaning: A rectangular area with side lengths x+a and x+b is modeled by their product and has square units.

validity_conditions: Use every relation only under its recorded conditions.
The linear-root relation applies only when the leading coefficient is non-zero.
The physical area relation additionally requires valid positive side lengths.
